blocks.x: What Applied AI & GenAI changes for FinTech & Digital Natives: the processes we target, the controls we inherit, the platforms underneath, and the measured delta at every gate.

FinTechs scale on decision speed: onboarding, fraud, credit and compliance must run real-time under regulatory scrutiny that grows with their size. The platforms that industrialize decisioning and evidence early avoid the mid-scale stall.

items: Onboarding drop-off at verification; completion suffers.
Ring fraud and account abuse scale faster than rules.

Governance inherits the sector frame — AML/CTF among others — with evidence generated by the delivery itself.

items: Align AI to P&L lines and risk mandates — a sequenced portfolio, not a pile of pilots.
One governed platform, many GenAI products: retrieval, guardrails and cost control as shared services.
Own your models: tune, distill and operate LLMs with measurable quality, controlled cost and enforceable policy.
Document/screening assembly with human gates (completion up)

blocks.x: At industry level, the same pattern

At Technology & SaaS level this capability reads as: eval apply, guardrails and cost telemetry wired into the product release train (AI features ship weekly with protected margin). The sub-industry page narrows it to the unit's workflows, regimes and KPIs.

This capability runs on the cadence set out below; the rhythm is fixed, the scope is signed. The first quarter of the rhythm is verification: weeks 1–2 measure the current metric with your team and lock it by signature. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with your control owner receiving evidence weekly. Weeks 9–12 industrialize: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and the measured delta against the signed baseline. Gates are binding: miss one and the program stops or redirects with a documented decision.
